newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico expects most votes counted mid-Monday.
newsitem.headline: Mexico expects most votes counted mid-Monday.

text.p: Mexico's independent Federal Electoral Institute (IFE) said on Friday it expects to have counted about 90 percent of the vote from Sunday's national elections by noon (1500 GMT) on Monday.
The IFE said about 35 percent of the vote would be known by 0200 local (0700 GMT) Monday morning.

Mexicans will vote for a new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time, the mayor of Mexico City. Previously, that post has been filled by a presidential nominee.
Although much faster than in previous years, the count will still be somewhat slow due to the intricate processing system, IFE preliminary election result coordinator Victor Guerra told reporters.

Votes are to be collected in 104,716 polling centers around the country with a 12-step procedure before being sent through a special 10-key keyboard computer to central district sites. The physical ballots follow, with signatures from the polls' top voting officials.

Guerra estimated the tabulation process will take about one to three hours, after polls close at 1800 local/2300 GMT. The more uncertain delay will be the physical transfer of the ballots to the regional districts, which in more rural states could take as long as four hours.
"It would be irresponsible for us to make guarantees. It could rain, there could be some other reason for delay," Guerra said. "We will make the results known as soon as we have them."

Mexico for the first time will make its election results public through the internet, beginning at 2000 Sunday (0100 GMT Monday). Data at the IFE home site (www.ife.org.mx) is to be updated every half hour.
The IFE will provide a back up computer for each transmission computer and back up data bases, "just in case," Guerra said.

The extra computers look to prevent events as in the 1988 presidential election, when the central computer collecting results halted with the opposition ahead. When it came back up hours later, the ruling party candidate was in the lead.
The IFE also said on Friday that 99.69 percent of the poll booths will have representatives from at least two political parties.
